policy: For every entities/entity_mentions/findings/sources/signal_* String(n) column, a test must fail if any writer whose value_origin is llm, external_api, scraped_html, rss, or user_input writes an un-truncated/un-validated value into it (decision must_widen or must_truncate below), and must also fail if any internally-derived literal string the code can assign to a column is itself longer than that column's declared width (see signal_results.result).
shape_notes: Added two coverage sub-fields not in the original shape: files_grep_checked (files searched for writers by grep but not opened in full) and files_not_examined (files in the corpus not inspected at all). Pure string_columns_total/columns_with_writers_traced/columns_unreached/files_read counters cannot show partial-confidence coverage, and this corpus has real writers living in scripts/ that a grep-only pass over app/ would miss entirely (see entities.domain, entities.registry_id, signal_results.result).

The target shape's example row is entity_mentions.role_hint, a column that is no longer String(n) (migration 007 widened it to Text). Kept it as columns[0] for continuity with the motivating bug, but it is excluded from coverage.string_columns_total (37, not 38) since the instruction was to enumerate String(n) columns and this one no longer is. Its 'decision' field is filled as ok_bounded ('unbounded now, so the failure mode cannot recur') for schema consistency only -- the 5-value decision enum has no clean label for 'already fixed, no longer in scope'; this is the same shape gap called out for signal_results.result below.

signal_results.result (see below) does not fit the given decision taxonomy cleanly: the offending value is not externally sourced, it is a hardcoded internal string literal ('not_applicable', 14 chars) that is longer than its own column (String(12)). must_widen was chosen because truncating a fixed enum-like literal would corrupt it rather than lose 'meaning' in the prose sense the rule describes, but the taxonomy's llm/external framing does not anticipate a column that is too narrow for its own code.

coverage.note: 64 .py files exist under app/, scripts/, alembic/ (excluding __pycache__). 35 were fully read, 14 grep-checked for model writes and confirmed clean (no ORM constructor / setattr / raw SQL touching mapped models), 12 not examined (tests, unrelated tooling, one JS shim, alembic/env.py boilerplate, database.py session plumbing, and llm.py which only wraps the model API call already traced via ops_client.call_llm).

columns.rationale: The MOTIVATING BUG. Was String(80); a 101-char and then a 123-char LLM-written role hint on consecutive nights caused asyncpg.StringDataRightTruncationError and killed the cron cycle (see alembic/versions/007_widen_role_hint.py:1-16, which documents both incidents). Migration 007 (alembic/versions/007_widen_role_hint.py:24-30) widened it to Text, so it no longer has a width and this class of failure cannot recur here. Kept in the contract as the reference case; see shape_notes for why 'decision' is a forced fit for an already-fixed column.

POST /api/sources is not behind verify_cron_secret or the console password (app/api/routes.py:63-67 has no auth dependency; only /tasks/* and /admin/* use verify_cron_secret per app/api/deps.py:17). SourceCreate.name (app/schemas.py:11) is a bare `str` with no Field(max_length=...), so an unauthenticated caller can insert a name of any length and hit the exact StringDataRightTruncationError class as the motivating bug. Separately, app/services/source_pipeline.py:191 feeds an un-truncated LLM-derived entity.display_name straight into Source.name when a self-grown source is created. The Notion reconcile path (app/services/notion_control.py:436,455) takes a page title verbatim from Notion's API with no length check either. Contrast: scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:437 truncates the same kind of value (`sname[:255]`) before insert, showing the codebase already knows the right fix for this exact field elsewhere.

page_id / page["id"] is Notion's own object id, always a UUID (36 chars incl. dashes) returned by the Notion REST API (app/services/notion_control.py:218-219, 255-262). Notion does not let a caller choose this id, so the value's format is bounded by Notion's own ID scheme, not by app-level validation. No truncation exists in code but none is needed at 36 <= 64.

Same unauthenticated POST /api/sources path as sources.name, plus a Notion 'select' property (app/services/notion_control.py:124-126) whose options are only a UI suggestion -- Notion lets a user add a new option with arbitrary text at edit time, which _extract_prop_text (app/services/notion_control.py:66-80) returns verbatim. Neither path validates against the two intended values (manual, self-grown) or the column width.

app/services/source_pipeline.py:83-89 asks an LLM (run_ops_json_prompt, agent='source-onboarder') to return a 'cadence_bucket' key and writes classification.get('cadence_bucket') straight through on line 106 with no membership check against the four allowed values (hourly, every_6_hours, daily, weekly listed in the prompt at source_pipeline.py:72) -- an off-script LLM answer is not truncated or rejected. The unauthenticated API and Notion select paths carry the same risk as sources.discovery_mode.

Longest known internal literal is 'bootstrap_pending' (18 chars, fits 30 comfortably), so the internal writers are safe today. The risk is the same unauthenticated POST /api/sources path (no max_length on app/schemas.py:22) and the Notion 'Initial Backfill Status' select field (app/services/notion_control.py:434,445), both unbounded.

Not a field on SourceBase/SourceCreate (app/schemas.py:10-23 has no auto_growth_state key), so `Source(**source.model_dump())` in app/api/routes.py:68 cannot set it -- unlike the other four sources.* string columns, the unauthenticated API route has no path to this column. Only writer found is the 9-char literal 'candidate'; default is 'manual' (app/models.py:132-134).

Only ever set to one of a small fixed set of code literals; longest is 'completed_with_errors' at 22 chars, which fits the current width of 30. alembic/versions/002_widen_scan_run_status.py:1-22 shows this column was already widened once (20 -> 30) for exactly this reason, so 30 is a deliberately-chosen bound, not an accident.

hashlib.sha256(...).hexdigest() always returns exactly 64 hex characters (app/sources/base.py:19-21), or the fetcher returns an empty string on error (app/sources/base.py:41-49). Both cases fit String(64) exactly.

RawFinding.category (app/pipeline/analyzer.py:27-30) is a bare Pydantic `str` with no max_length and no Literal[...] constraint, even though the system prompt tells the LLM to pick one of 8 short tokens (app/pipeline/analyzer.py:64: 'category: funding_round, product_launch, partnership, regulatory, hiring, research, market_move, opinion'). app/pipeline/scorer.py:166-171 spreads raw_finding unchanged (`**raw_finding`), and app/pipeline/orchestrator.py:303 writes it straight into the column. Nothing in the chain enforces the 8-value vocabulary or a length bound; a model that answers with a longer descriptive string instead of one of the 8 tokens overflows the column exactly like the motivating bug. Unlike role_hint this is meant to be a short controlled token, so truncating is the semantically-correct fix (validating against FINDING_CATEGORIES, which exists in app/models.py:52-61 but is never enforced at the DB or Pydantic layer, is a decision left to open_questions).
sha256(...).hexdigest() is always exactly 64 hex characters; fits String(64) exactly with no slack.
Same Notion-generated UUID pattern as sources.notion_page_id and watch_targets.notion_page_id; 36 chars, not caller-controlled.

No explicit writer found anywhere in app/ or scripts/ (Evidence(...) is constructed in app/pipeline/orchestrator.py:319-325, scripts/import_scan_data.py:69-74, and scripts/seed_demo_fixtures.py:191-197, and none of the three pass content_type). Every row therefore takes the column default 'text' (app/models.py:264-266). This is the one column in the corpus with confirmed zero explicit application-level writers -- counted as columns_unreached rather than columns_with_writers_traced, since 'traced' here means only 'confirmed no writer exists' rather than 'followed a writer to its source'.

All dedup_key writers are f-strings over a fixed prefix + integer id(s) + either a short literal or an ISO timestamp / sha256 hexdigest. Worst case observed is app/api/routes.py:183-188 ('notion_webhook:' [15 chars] + a 64-char sha256 hexdigest = 79 chars), which fits 128. No caller passes raw external text into this field.

Named explicitly in the task brief as the same shape as the motivating bug. `name` (app/services/agent_pipeline.py:298) comes from raw_entities, which is either _extract_entities_with_agent (an LLM call, agent='entity-extractor', app/services/agent_pipeline.py:159-185) or, when known entities are skipped, _heuristic_extract_entities (app/services/agent_pipeline.py:124-156), which itself pulls from finding.metadata_['entities'] -- populated from RawFinding.entities (app/pipeline/analyzer.py:35), also LLM output -- or a regex over finding.title, whose text is itself LLM-written. Every path terminates at LLM-generated text. No length check exists before either constructor call (line 206) or the update-path assignment (line 216). Unlike role_hint this is a name field (a person or company name), so per the given decision rule ('bounded width is semantically right (e.g. a name)') truncating rather than widening is the correct fix -- 255 chars is already generous for a real entity name, and the codebase truncates neighboring free-text fields in the same function (description=finding.summary[:500] on line 313, context_excerpt=finding.summary[:500] on line 346) but not this one.

normalize_name() (app/services/agent_pipeline.py:69-70) collapses runs of non-alphanumeric characters to a single space and lowercases -- it can only shorten or preserve the input length, never lengthen it. Its input is the same un-truncated LLM `name` traced under entities.display_name, so normalized_name carries an identical, un-mitigated overflow risk and the same fix applies.

No writer exists anywhere in app/ (grep for '.domain' / 'domain=' under app/ only matches read sites in app/api/console.py:100,536); the column is currently only ever populated by the one-off script scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py, which reads candidate.json research data written by an external discovery/scoring process and computes `host_of(url) = urlparse(...).netloc.lower()` (scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:61-65). If the source 'domain' field is not really URL-shaped (no '/','?','#' delimiter), urlparse's netloc extraction is not length-bounded, so this is not provably truncated -- see open_questions for whether this offline path is in scope at all.

Same situation as entities.domain: no writer anywhere in app/ (the only app/ reference is a read of a DIFFERENT value at app/api/console.py:537, which pulls 'registry_id' out of entity.metadata_['stratum3'], not this column). The only writer is scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py, which inserts cand.get('registry_id') from external research data with no length check on either the UPDATE (line 237-264) or INSERT (line 267-296) path.

writers.excerpt: (scan_id, sig_id, verdict, (sig.get("url") or "")[:1000] or None, (sig.get("evidence") or "")[:1000] or None, sig_points if verdict == "confirmed" else 0.0),

columns.rationale: HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING. "not_applicable" is 14 characters (n-o-t-_-a-p-p-l-i-c-a-b-l-e), but signal_results.result is String(12) (app/models.py:639) -- a valid, code-defined value for this column is itself 2 characters longer than the column can hold. This is not an external-input problem: RESULT_CREDIT/UNSCORED_RESULTS (app/services/signal_engine.py:175-177) treat 'not_applicable' as a first-class valid result, and app/services/signal_engine.py:471 writes item['result'] (which compute_scan_scoring can set to 'not_applicable' whenever an LLM batch answers '?' mapped via a caller-supplied verdict, or more directly whenever _parse_batch_results (app/services/signal_engine.py:366-386) sees an 'na'/'n/a' verdict token, app/services/signal_engine.py:371-372) with no length check. There is also a SEPARATE, already-exercised writer: scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:131,368-382 maps 'NA' -> 'not_applicable' via its own VERDICT_MAP and inserts it directly into signal_results.result via raw SQL with no truncation (line 369-373), under PROVENANCE 'stratum3-manual-scan-2026-07-30' (scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:35) -- i.e. this is not hypothetical, it is a value the codebase's own manual-import tool is known to have attempted to write to production. Truncating 'not_applicable' to 12 chars would silently corrupt a value multiple call sites compare for equality (e.g. counts['not_applicable'] downstream logic), so the column must be widened, not the value truncated -- the reverse of every other finding in this contract.
Only 'active' (6 chars) or 'watch' (5 chars) are ever written; default is also 'active' (app/models.py:665-667).
Same Notion-generated UUID pattern as sources.notion_page_id and findings.notion_page_id.

open_questions.question: signal_results.result is String(12) but the code's own fixed vocabulary includes 'not_applicable' (14 chars), which multiple writers can produce (app/services/signal_engine.py:176,371-372,471 and scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:131,368-382 -- the latter under a PROVENANCE tag showing it already ran against production once). Should the column be widened (e.g. to 20, mirroring the pattern already used for signal_scans.band per alembic/versions/006_entity_typing_and_gate.py:83-89's 'insufficient-evidence' fix), or should the code-level vocabulary use a shorter token (e.g. 'n_a' or 'na') instead?
open_questions.evidence_for_widen: alembic/versions/006_entity_typing_and_gate.py:83-89 already widened signal_scans.band from 20 to 30 for the identical reason (a literal in code was longer than the column); the same fix pattern applies directly.
open_questions.evidence_for_shorter_token: Every other value in the vocabulary (confirmed, absent, unknown) is <=9 chars; only 'not_applicable' is an outlier, so shrinking the one token is a smaller diff than widening the column, but touches every downstream string comparison against 'not_applicable' (at least app/services/signal_engine.py:176,196,202,212,222,224,230,266-267 and console.py display code).

open_questions.question: POST /api/sources (app/api/routes.py:63-80) has no auth dependency and SourceCreate (app/schemas.py:10-27) has no Field(max_length=...) or Literal[...] constraints on any of these four string fields. Should the fix be (a) Pydantic max_length matching the DB width (prevents the crash, still allows garbage up to N chars), (b) Literal/enum validation against the actual allowed vocabularies (cadence_bucket in {hourly,every_6_hours,daily,weekly}, discovery_mode in {manual,self-grown}, onboarding_status against a defined set) -- which fixes both the crash and invalid-value risk, or (c) adding auth to the route, which is an orthogonal but adjacent gap?
open_questions.evidence: app/api/deps.py:17-22 defines verify_cron_secret and only /tasks/* and /admin/* routes use it (app/api/routes.py:216-291); /api/sources (both GET and POST) has zero Depends() auth.

open_questions.question: scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py is the ONLY writer found anywhere in the corpus for entities.domain and entities.registry_id, and is a second writer (alongside the live agent pipeline) for signal_results.result. It is a manually-invoked, --dry-run/--commit gated script, not part of the deployed Railway image's request/worker cycle, and it hardcodes a full production Postgres connection string with a plaintext password at scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:34. Should this script's writes count as in-scope 'reachable from LLM output' risk for this contract (as this analysis treated them), or should offline/manual data-ops tooling be tracked in a separate contract since it is not part of the always-running service the motivating bug (a cron cycle dying every night) describes?
open_questions.evidence: scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:1-13 docstring: 'Import discovered + scored companies and their sources into production... Usage: python3 import_to_db.py --dry-run / --commit'; DSN at line 34 points to switchback.proxy.rlwy.net, a Railway proxy host, i.e. production.

open_questions.question: Not a column-width issue, flagged because it was found while tracing writers: scripts/sourcing_run/import_to_db.py:34 hardcodes a live production Postgres DSN including a plaintext password ('postgresql://postgres:<REDACTED>@switchback.proxy.rlwy.net:16120/railway'), committed to the repository. Out of scope for this contract's policy but severe enough to surface for a human decision on rotation/removal.
